<!-- Generated from the design document, Build order tab, revision 47 (2026-10-27). Do not edit: see docs/intent/INDEX.md. -->
**Rules for the builder.**

- **One item at a time, in order.** If an item is blocked, write down why in the progress file and go on to the next item that does not depend on it.
- **Branches.** Work on a `develop` branch, created from `main` if it does not exist. Each item gets its own branch from `develop`, its own tests and its own report. When the tests pass and one reviewer has found nothing blocking, merge the item into `develop` and go on. Never push to `main`: it changes only by merging the milestone pull request from `develop`, which the builder merges itself once CI is green (decided 27 October 2026, Haakon: "You merge, always.").
- **The specification** is the sections each item names, in this document and in `docs/rounds/2026-10-18-sleep-and-simulation.md` (the old round report, whose "question N" plans many items refer to). Read the rest of the document for intent only; build nothing outside the item. The document keeps changing while you work, so builders read it from its copy in the repository (decided 26 October 2026): `docs/intent/`, one file per section, cut from a stated revision of this document and refreshed after each design session. When starting an item, ask the live document for what changed since that revision; where the two differ, the live document wins. Ask again before opening the item's pull request (decided 27 October 2026), since Haakon's answers to earlier items' questions often change it while it is being built: build what changed that the item touches, or, if that is large, say so in the pull request and add it to the start of the next item that touches it.
- **Every rule a king needs is in the rulebook or the seat view,** changed in the same commit as the rule. The design notes (`docs/design/`, indexed by `docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md`) are updated in the same commit too.
- **Requests are rules too** (decided 20 October 2026). Models read their requests literally, so every field is a nudge: no field may imply something that is not true. A question about "the carried gold" when none is carried made an envoy claim gold he did not have, and an internal number ("k8") became "the peace of turn eight" sealed into a tablet. Ask only what applies, show no internal ids or numbers a king or character could repeat, and keep the engine's outcomes apart from a character's own words.
- **Balance: first guesses during the build, tuning at the end** (decided 19 October 2026). Balance stays frozen in every item. Where an item adds numbers of its own (times, costs, odds, thresholds), set reasonable first guesses that keep games playable, list them in the item's report, and do not tune them: later items change the pace of the game, so tuning each system as it arrives is wasted, and the balance pass (item 18) tunes everything together. The one exception is anything that makes games unplayable for testing, such as a capital falling within two seasons, which the item fixes. Run the bot benchmarks after every item as a regression check, never to tune. Seeds replay exactly within a save version; new rules mean a new save version.
- **No rule checks which power it is** ("Different data, same rules"). Asymmetry comes from the map and starting data; only presentation and voice (season names, titles, greetings, gift lines) may name a power.
- **No model games until the build order is done** (decided 20 October 2026). Games with model kings or characters cost weekly usage and say little about a build that lacks the features they would test, so none are run until every item is built, and then only when Haakon asks. Script games and stand-in repliers check everything until then. When model games return, every debrief, for kings and characters alike, also asks: "What did you find most and least interesting about playing this role?" A role an agent finds dull probably has too few real choices, so the answers are design data. Add the question to the simulation kit's debriefs when next working on it, so it is ready. Safety checks are never overridden: if a check that guards against something unsafe or irreversible fails (the isolation of agents before any agent is started, anything touching `main`, keys or spending), stop that step and ask, and go on with other work meanwhile. The simulation kit's start prompt, which is what an orchestrator actually reads, repeats this rule in the same words; add it there when next working on the kit. An ordinary failing test is not a reason to stop: fix it, or mark the item blocked with the reason and go on to the next item that does not depend on it.
- **Script kings and script characters are the sparring partners and the balance proxy** (decided 20 October 2026). They are to play as competently as possible, since strong bots reveal weaknesses in the rules and give the balance pass something worth measuring.
  - **Every item tests them.** After each item, play script games on its new rules, alongside the benchmarks, and look for weaknesses in the bots' play: a rule they never use, an exploit they fall for or never try, an order or errand that keeps failing, a choice a competent player would not make. On the same seeds, play scripts that use the item's feature against scripts that ignore it: if using it does not win, either the feature does not matter or the scripts play it badly, and the report says which (decided 21 October 2026). The item's report lists what was found.
  - **Every weakness found is patched** in the item at hand, for kings and characters alike, with the benchmarks recorded before and after. A new rule is not finished until the script kings and characters can use it well. This is the tenet "Every feature is every seat's": the report shows, for each feature the item adds, how often script players used it and how often it succeeded, and a feature they never use, or use without ever succeeding, is not done. Once, at the start of the next item begun, audit every feature built so far the same way, and patch the gaps (as the fix pass after item 4 did for script kings never examining the inventory tablets that travel with gold).
  - **Improving their play is allowed in every item,** as an exception to frozen balance; tuning the game's own numbers still waits for item 18.
- **A pull request at every milestone** (decided 20 October 2026). Each time an item is merged into `develop`, push `develop` and make sure a PR from `develop` to `main` carries it, and merge it once CI is green, so each item reaches the live game and Haakon can test it there. Before pushing, check the state of the previous PR: if it is still open, the push adds to it; if it was merged, first merge `main` back into `develop` (whatever way the PR was merged), then push and open a new PR. Never push to a branch whose PR was merged without that check.
- **Unattended work.** Don't stop to ask: where something is ambiguous, take the most reasonable reading, write it down, and carry on. Stop only before anything irreversible.
- **Progress.** Keep `docs/BUILD-PROGRESS.md` in the repository: one line per item with its state (not started, in progress, done, blocked), its branch, its report, and anything decided along the way. Each item's report goes to `docs/rounds/<date>-<item>.md`.
- **Usage.** Be economical: one reviewer per item, no extra analyst workflows unless a result looks wrong. Work continuously, item after item, and check weekly usage after every commit. Haakon (26 October 2026): "I want these 2 continually working until they reach about 90% usage, at that point I don't want them taking on any bigger task, as I want the bulk of that remaining usage for myself." So from about 90% of the weekly limit, take on no bigger task: finish the item at hand if it is nearly done, or bring it to a clean commit and open a draft pull request saying how to test it and what is left; then only small things, with the progress file up to date. "These 2" are this game's builder and Barkstreet Snakes'.
- **Review points do not stop the build** (decided 20 October 2026). The whole build order is to be built. For an item marked "Stop for review", finish it, write its review questions and the readings taken in its report, list them at the top of the progress file for Haakon, and go on to the next item. Stop only before anything irreversible, when a safety check fails ("No model games until the build order is done"), or as "Usage" says once usage nears 90% of the week.
- **No stopgaps (decided 21 October 2026).** Where an item comes before a feature it would want, the built game stays as it is until that feature's item, and the item says so: letters travel by themselves until item 11b, gold reaches the treasury at once until item 13, a mutinous unit disbands until bands exist. Such notes cost nothing and tell the builder what not to build yet. What is never done is inventing a rule for the meantime: if an item would need a new rule only because a later item is missing, the order is wrong, and the lever moves to the item that brings its consequence, or the later feature moves forward. A lever and its counterweight are built together: the king's tax rate comes with the hunger that answers it (item 10+a), and city-states come early (item 11+) instead of being stood in for until the end of the order. The order serves the finished game, not the other way round (Haakon, 27 October 2026: "the build order is simply to guideline claude code. I only care about the final product and that we don't introduce temporary features"): where an item's order or split serves the game badly, take the reading that builds the final game best and say so in the PR.
